In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the control mechanism for the vortex generators in this case is the interaction between the vortex generator and the suction-side boundary layer.
the control of separation is achieved by the formation of a strong vortex in the separation region, which is generated by the interaction of the vortex generators and the boundary-layer flow.

the control is very effective in delaying separation and that the mechanism involves an increase in the suction-skin-friction level and a decrease in the suction-surface pressure gradient, which is a result of the vortex-generator-jet-induced streamwise vorticity and the corresponding spanwise flow.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the flow physics of the control is more complicated than the simple idea of blowing vortices into the separation bubble.
the pulsed vortex generator jet does not simply delay the onset of laminar separation, but rather causes a transition to turbulence.

the pulsed jets do not act directly on the separation region, as has been suggested in the past, but instead they trigger a global mode in the blade wake that is responsible for the separation-control effect.
